why: I checked each verifier check's PASS/FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Checks 1 and 2 only test concrete cases of the stated behaviour (for example '42',5,'0'→'00042' and '12345',5→unchanged), so they are fine. Check 3's demand for "text describing it" under each heading is borderline but defensible as part of having a section. Check 4 breaks the criterion. "npm test passes" only needs a zero exit, but the PASS condition also requires that "the summary shows `# fail 0`". That is an exact-wording requirement on the output. It depends on the TAP reporter: newer Node versions' spec reporter prints "ℹ fail 0" instead. So a passing test run could still be marked FAIL. This stricter condition belongs under Advisory, not in the PASS condition.
